title: Dropping a single-line work order on a technician cell creates a shift immediately, skipping the scope picker
permissions_required: Schedule: Edit (requires View) + Work Orders: View for the sidebar (spec §14.1, §14.2).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A ZZAUTOTEST work order exists with exactly ONE approved line whose estimated hours fit within one working day of the target technician.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
steps: 1. Drag that work order's card from the sidebar.
2. Drop it onto a technician's cell on a working day.
expected: 1. A shift is created immediately in that cell - no scope picker and no spread step appears.
2. The shift block shows the customer name, unit number, and the line's name.
3. The technician is added to that line's labor roster on the work order.
4. A toast with an Undo option appears.

title: Dropping a multi-line work order on a technician cell opens the scope picker
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A work order exists with TWO or more approved lines.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
steps: 1. Drag that work order's card from the sidebar.
2. Drop it onto a technician's cell.
expected: 1. A scope picker popover opens, anchored to the cell you dropped on.
2. It offers 'Schedule whole work order' at the top, the individual line rows beneath, and a 'Select multiple' control.
3. No shift is created until a scope is chosen.

title: Dragging an individual line from the drill-down creates a single-line shift directly
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A work order with several approved lines exists; its drill-down is open in the sidebar.
3. The chosen line's hours fit within one working day of the target technician.
4. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
steps: 1. Using the line's drag handle, drag one specific line from the drill-down.
2. Drop it onto a technician's cell.
expected: 1. A single-line shift for exactly that line is created directly - no scope picker appears.
2. The block's last text line shows that line's name.
3. The technician is added to that line's roster only (not to the order's other lines).

title: A job exceeding the technician's daily hours opens the spread step after the scope is chosen
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A ZZAUTOTEST work order exists whose chosen scope's estimated hours EXCEED one working day of the target technician (for example a 40h line for a tech with 8h days).
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
steps: 1. Drag the work order (or the large line) onto a technician's cell.
2. If the scope picker opens, choose the large scope.
3. Look at what opens next.
expected: 1. The spread step opens (step 2 of the same modal) to distribute the hours across consecutive working days.
2. Its header shows the chosen scope and a 'Change scope' back-link.
3. No shifts exist yet until the spread is confirmed.

title: A scope that fits within one working day skips the spread step and creates a single shift
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A multi-line work order exists where one line's hours fit within the target technician's working day.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
steps: 1. Drag the work order onto a technician's cell.
2. In the scope picker, tap the small line.
expected: 1. The shift is created straight away - the spread step does NOT appear.
2. The shift sits on the dropped day only.

title: While dragging, drop-target cells highlight and a ghost block shows the line name and hours
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A work order with an approved line exists.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
steps: 1. Start dragging a line from the sidebar and hold it over different grid cells without dropping.
2. Watch the cell under the cursor and the dragged preview.
expected: 1. The cell currently under the cursor highlights as a drop target.
2. A ghost block follows the drag showing the line name and its hours.
3. Releasing outside any valid cell creates nothing.
notes: Highlight and ghost styling unpinned (no designs) - confirm the visuals live. The cancel-outside-cell behavior is a reasonable derivation, not spec-stated - confirm live.

title: Scheduling a technician onto a line adds them to that line's labor roster on the work order
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A work order exists with an approved line where the target technician is NOT yet on the line's roster.
3. You are on the Schedule page.
steps: 1. Drag that line onto the technician's cell and create the shift.
2. Open the same work order's line (in the sidebar drill-down and/or on the Work Orders page) and check its technician roster.
expected: 1. The technician now appears on that line's labor roster - the schedule and the work order stay in sync automatically.
2. The sidebar line row's avatar stack/count updates to include the technician.
3. If the line previously showed 'Needs techs', the badge is gone.

title: A click-to-arm alternative exists for scheduling without dragging
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A work order with an approved line exists.
3. You are on the Schedule page.
steps: 1. Instead of dragging, click (arm) the work order card or line in the sidebar.
2. Then click a technician cell in the grid.
expected: 1. The item can be placed onto a cell without holding a drag - clicking arms it, and clicking a cell places it.
2. The result is the same as the equivalent drag-and-drop (scope picker / spread step rules apply the same way).
notes: The spec requires a click-to-arm alternative but does not pin the exact interaction (what arms, how disarm/cancel works) - capture the real mechanics live.

title: 'Schedule whole work order' is pinned at the top, visually distinct, labeled with line count and total hours
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A work order exists with three approved lines with known estimated hours.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
steps: 1. Drag the work order onto a technician's cell to open the scope picker.
2. Read the top option.
expected: 1. The 'Schedule whole work order' option sits pinned at the top of the picker and looks visually distinct from the line rows.
2. It is labeled with the order's line count and total hours (matching the sum of the approved lines).
3. The picker is anchored to the cell that was dropped on.
notes: 'Schedule whole work order' is the spec's wording - confirm the exact on-screen label and the count/hours format live.

title: Choosing 'Schedule whole work order' assigns the technician to all lines and creates one whole-order shift
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A ZZAUTOTEST work order exists with two or more approved lines whose TOTAL hours fit within the technician's working day (to avoid the spread step).
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
steps: 1. Drag the work order onto a technician's cell.
2. Choose 'Schedule whole work order'.
3. Check the created block and the work order's line rosters.
expected: 1. One shift is created covering all of the order's approved lines.
2. The block's last text line reads 'N Lines' (with N = the line count).
3. The technician is added to the roster of every one of those lines.

title: Tapping an individual line row immediately creates a single-line shift with no confirmation step
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A multi-line work order exists; one line fits within the technician's day.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
steps: 1. Drag the work order onto a technician's cell.
2. In the scope picker, click one line row (do not use 'Select multiple').
expected: 1. A single-line shift for that line is created immediately - no extra confirmation step.
2. The picker closes.
3. The block's last text line shows the line's name.

title: Scope picker line rows show the line title, estimated hours, and current technician roster
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A multi-line work order exists where at least one line already has technicians on its roster.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
steps: 1. Drag the work order onto a technician's cell to open the scope picker.
2. Read each line row.
expected: 1. Each row shows the line title and its estimated hours.
2. Rows for lines that already have technicians show the current roster as an avatar stack plus count.

title: 'Select multiple' switches rows to checkboxes with a confirm bar showing a running tally
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A work order exists with three or more approved lines.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
steps: 1. Drag the work order onto a technician's cell.
2. Click 'Select multiple'.
3. Tick two lines and read the confirm bar.
4. Confirm.
expected: 1. The line rows switch into checkbox mode.
2. A confirm bar appears with a running tally of the selection - the count of lines and their combined hours (in the spec's example format, 'Create shift · 2 lines · 6h').
3. Confirming creates ONE shift covering the ticked lines, and the technician is added to those lines' rosters only.
notes: 'Select multiple' and the tally format 'Create shift · 2 lines · 6h' are the spec's wording - confirm the exact on-screen labels/format live.

title: 'Select all' equals whole order; Cancel returns to the fast single-tap list
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A multi-line work order exists.
3. You are on the Schedule page with the scope picker open in 'Select multiple' mode.
steps: 1. Click 'Select all' and read the tally.
2. Click Cancel instead of confirming.
3. Look at the picker.
expected: 1. 'Select all' ticks every line - the tally equals the whole order (same line count and hours as 'Schedule whole work order').
2. Cancel leaves checkbox mode and returns to the normal single-tap line list without creating anything.
notes: 'Select all' / 'Cancel' are the spec's words - confirm the exact on-screen labels live.

area: Shift Start Times and Unassigned Shifts
title: A shift's start time uses the technician's configured working hours when they are set
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A technician has configured working hours that DIFFER from the shop's business hours (for example tech 6:00 AM start vs shop 8:00 AM) - set this up first and restore after.
3. A schedulable work order line exists.
4. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
steps: 1. Drop the line onto that technician's cell (week view - not a day-view timeline drop).
2. Open the created shift's detail and read its start time.
expected: 1. The shift starts at the technician's own configured start time (6:00 AM in the example), not the shop's business-hours start.

area: Shift Start Times and Unassigned Shifts
title: With no technician hours set, the shift start time falls back to the shop's business hours
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A technician exists with NO configured working hours, and the shop HAS business hours set (note the shop start time).
3. A schedulable work order line exists.
4. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
steps: 1. Drop the line onto that technician's cell.
2. Read the created shift's start time.
expected: 1. The shift starts at the shop's business-hours start time.

area: Shift Start Times and Unassigned Shifts
title: With neither technician hours nor business hours set, a 7:00 AM default applies
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A technician exists with no configured hours AND the shop's business hours are not set (adjust settings if the environment allows; restore the settings byte-identical after).
3. A schedulable work order line exists.
4. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
steps: 1. Drop the line onto that technician's cell.
2. Read the created shift's start time.
expected: 1. The shift starts at 7:00 AM - the general default working day (7:00 AM to 7:00 PM) applies.
notes: 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM default is spec-stated - confirm the actual default live. If business hours cannot be unset in the environment, mark blocked with reason rather than skipping silently.

area: Shift Start Times and Unassigned Shifts
title: In day view, the start time comes from where the shift is dropped on the timeline
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A schedulable work order line exists.
3. You are on the Schedule page in DAY view.
steps: 1. Drag the line from the sidebar and drop it at a specific time position on a technician's timeline (for example around 10:00 AM).
2. Read the created shift's start time.
expected: 1. The shift starts at the time position where it was dropped (not at the technician-hours/business-hours default).
2. The start time aligns to the timeline position (see the 15-minute snapping case SCH-DAY-04).

area: Shift Start Times and Unassigned Shifts
title: Dropping a work order or line onto the Unassigned row creates an unassigned shift with no technician
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A schedulable work order line exists.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
steps: 1. Drag the line from the sidebar and drop it onto the grid's Unassigned row on a working day.
2. Look at the created block and the line's roster.
expected: 1. An unassigned shift is created in the Unassigned row for that day.
2. It has no technician (and no technician is added to the line's roster by this drop).
3. The block uses the same anatomy as a regular shift (customer, unit, line name / 'N Lines').
notes: The spec does not explicitly state whether the roster stays untouched until assignment - derived from 'they simply have no technician yet'; confirm the roster behavior live.

area: Shift Start Times and Unassigned Shifts
title: Unassigned shift start time skips the technician-hours rule and uses business hours or the default
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. The shop has business hours set (note the start time).
3. A schedulable work order line exists.
4. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
steps: 1. Drop the line onto the Unassigned row.
2. Read the created shift's start time.
expected: 1. The unassigned shift starts at the shop's business-hours start (there is no technician whose hours could apply).
2. If the shop had no business hours, it would start at the 7:00 AM default.

area: Shift Start Times and Unassigned Shifts
title: Dragging an unassigned shift onto a technician row assigns it, and that technician's hours then apply
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. An unassigned shift exists in the Unassigned row.
3. The target technician has configured working hours that differ from the shop's business hours.
4. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
steps: 1. Drag the unassigned shift from the Unassigned row down onto a technician's row.
2. Check the shift and the line's roster.
expected: 1. The shift is now assigned to that technician (it leaves the Unassigned row and sits in the technician's row).
2. The technician is added to the affected line's roster.
3. The technician's own working hours now apply to the shift's timing.
notes: Whether the start time re-derives on assignment or keeps its original time is not fully pinned ('that technician's hours apply') - capture the exact behavior live.

area: Shift Start Times and Unassigned Shifts
title: Every shift always has a start time - none is created without one
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. Work order lines are available to schedule.
3. You are on the Schedule page.
steps: 1. Create shifts by each entry point available: week-view drop on a technician, day-view drop on the timeline, drop on the Unassigned row.
2. Open each created shift's detail and read its start time.
expected: 1. Every created shift has a concrete start time - resolved from the hierarchy (technician hours, then business hours, then 7:00 AM default) or from the day-view drop position.
2. No shift appears on the grid without a time.

title: Spread step shows the chosen scope in its header with a 'Change scope' back-link
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A multi-line work order exists with a scope that exceeds the technician's daily hours.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
steps: 1. Drop the work order on a technician, choose the large scope, and reach the spread step.
2. Read the spread step's header.
expected: 1. The spread step appears as step 2 of the same modal.
2. Its header shows the chosen scope (which lines / how many hours).
3. A 'Change scope' back-link is present.
notes: 'Change scope' is the spec's wording - confirm the exact on-screen label live.

title: 'Change scope' returns from the spread step to the scope picker
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. You are on the spread step (step 2) for a multi-line work order.
steps: 1. Click 'Change scope'.
2. Choose a different scope and continue.
expected: 1. The modal goes back to the scope picker (step 1) without creating anything.
2. Choosing a new scope updates the spread step's header and hours accordingly.

title: How-much selector defaults to Full estimate; Full estimate, 1 week, and 2 weeks apply immediately with no extra fields
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. You are on the spread step for a large scope (for example 40+ hours).
steps: 1. Read the 'how much to schedule' selector's default value.
2. Open the selector and read its options.
3. Pick '1 week', then '2 weeks', then back to 'Full estimate', watching for extra fields.
expected: 1. The selector defaults to 'Full estimate'.
2. The options include 'Full estimate', '1 week', '2 weeks', 'Until a date…', and 'Specific hours…'.
3. 'Full estimate', '1 week', and '2 weeks' apply on selection with no extra fields - the modal stays to one line for these.
4. The preview summary updates to match each selection.
notes: Option labels ('Full estimate', '1 week', '2 weeks', 'Until a date…', 'Specific hours…') are the spec's wording - confirm the exact on-screen labels live.

title: 'Until a date…' reveals a single finish-by date field
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. You are on the spread step for a large scope.
steps: 1. Open the how-much selector and choose 'Until a date…'.
2. Look at the modal.
3. Pick a finish-by date.
expected: 1. Choosing 'Until a date…' reveals a single 'finish by' date field (this is the only custom control shown).
2. Picking a date updates the preview so the series ends by that date.
notes: What happens when the full estimate cannot fit by the chosen date is not specified - observe and record the actual behavior live; raise a PO question if ambiguous.

title: 'Specific hours…' reveals an hours stepper
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. You are on the spread step for a large scope.
steps: 1. Open the how-much selector and choose 'Specific hours…'.
2. Set a number of hours with the stepper (for example 16).
expected: 1. Choosing 'Specific hours…' reveals an hours stepper control.
2. The preview updates to spread exactly the entered hours across working days.
notes: Stepper bounds/increments not specified - capture live.

title: Start date defaults to the earliest working day and can be adjusted to make a second technician sequential
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A large job has already been spread for technician A (note A's series end date).
3. You are on the spread step for the SAME work order dropped on technician B.
steps: 1. Read the start-date field's default.
2. Change the start date to the day after technician A's series ends.
3. Confirm the spread.
expected: 1. The start date defaults to the earliest working day.
2. It can be changed; technician B's series then starts after A's series ends (sequential, not parallel).
3. B's series is created from the adjusted start date onward.

title: Spread uses the technician's own working hours and skips weekends and shop closures - the end date is emergent
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. The technician has known daily working hours (for example 8h/day, Monday to Friday).
3. A shop closure day is defined inside the spread window (set one up if the environment allows).
4. A scope of known size exists (for example 40h).
steps: 1. Spread the 40h scope for that technician with 'Full estimate' starting on a Monday.
2. Confirm and inspect the created shifts on the grid.
expected: 1. Daily shifts are sized to the technician's own working hours (8h each in the example).
2. No shifts are placed on Saturday, Sunday, or the shop closure day.
3. The end date is a result of the daily distribution (for 40h at 8h/day starting Monday with one closure, the series extends one extra working day).
notes: How shop closures are configured in the app is not described in this spec - locate the closure setting live; if closures cannot be configured, mark that expectation blocked with reason.

title: Preview is collapsed to a one-line summary, expandable to a week-by-week breakdown with skipped days struck through and their reasons
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. You are on the spread step for a multi-week scope that will skip at least one weekend.
steps: 1. Read the preview area without expanding it.
2. Expand the preview.
3. Find a skipped day in the breakdown.
expected: 1. Collapsed: a one-line summary in the spirit of the spec's example '20 shifts · Jun 15 to Jul 13 · skips weekends + 2 days'.
2. Expanded: a week-by-week breakdown of the planned shifts.
3. Skipped days are struck through and show the reason they are skipped (weekend / closure).
notes: The one-line summary format is the spec's example - confirm the real copy format live.

title: Confirming the spread creates a linked series of daily shifts
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. You are on the spread step for a multi-day scope with the preview showing several shifts.
steps: 1. Confirm the spread.
2. Look at the grid across the affected days/weeks.
3. Open one of the created shifts.
expected: 1. One daily shift is created per planned working day, together forming a linked series.
2. The shifts render as one connected banner (see the series-banner cases SCH-SER-01..03).
3. Each daily shift keeps its own day and hours.
4. A toast with Undo appears.

title: Dropping the same work order on a second technician spreads the full estimate again, independently
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A large work order (for example 40h) has already been fully spread for technician A.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
steps: 1. Drop the SAME work order onto technician B and complete the spread with 'Full estimate'.
2. Compare the two series.
expected: 1. Technician B gets a full 40h series of their own - the estimate is spread again in full, not reduced by A's booking.
2. There is no shared 'remaining hours' counter across technicians and no splitting of a shift.
3. Planned hours across technicians may now exceed the estimate - this is expected and produces no error (progress is driven by clocked-in time).

title: Month view renders a series as a continuous banner wrapping across week rows, labeled once, with a faded 'continues' label on later weeks
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. A multi-week series exists for one technician (spread a 40h+ job first).
3. You are on the Schedule page in MONTH view showing the series' month.
steps: 1. Find the series on the month grid.
2. Read the banner across the week rows.
3. Look at the weekend columns and any skipped or booked days inside the series.
expected: 1. The series renders as one continuous bar wrapping across the week rows.
2. It is labeled once at the start (including the technician); later weeks show a faded 'continues'-style label instead of repeating the full label.
3. Weekend columns inside the series are empty (no bar).
4. Visible breaks appear around skipped days and days the technician is otherwise booked.
notes: Exact banner styling and the 'continues' label wording unpinned (no designs) - confirm the visuals/copy live.

title: Week view renders a series as one banner spanning the week's working days, with edge chevrons and a 'week N of M' cue
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. A multi-week series exists for one technician; on one of its days the technician also has an unrelated booking.
3. You are on the Schedule page in WEEK view on a middle week of the series.
steps: 1. Find the series banner in the technician's row.
2. Look at the banner's left and right edges.
3. Look for the week-position cue and at the day with the other booking.
expected: 1. One banner spans the working days of that week in the technician's row.
2. Chevrons at the banner's edges indicate the series continues beyond the visible week (both sides, on a middle week).
3. A 'week N of M' cue shows the position within the series.
4. The banner breaks around the day the technician is otherwise booked.
notes: 'week N of M' is the spec's format - confirm the exact on-screen cue wording live.

title: Day view shows the series day as a single time-positioned block with a 'part of an M-week job' cue
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. A multi-week series exists for one technician.
3. You are on the Schedule page in DAY view on one of the series' days.
steps: 1. Find the series' block on the technician's timeline.
2. Read its cue text.
expected: 1. The day shows a single time-positioned block (no spanning bar - only one day is visible).
2. The block carries a cue in the spirit of 'part of an M-week job' indicating it belongs to a longer series.
notes: 'part of an M-week job' is the spec's phrasing - confirm the exact cue wording live.

title: A series is a grouping of ordinary daily shifts - capacity, overtime, and conflicts operate on the individual shifts
permissions_required: Schedule: View to observe; Schedule: Edit to set up (spec §14.1).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. A series exists for a technician; on one series day the technician also has a second, overlapping shift (set up with Edit permission).
3. Capacity Bars are on in View Options.
steps: 1. Look at the capacity bar of a day inside the series.
2. Look at the day with the overlapping second shift.
3. Open one series shift's detail.
expected: 1. Each series day contributes its own daily hours to that day's capacity bar (the series is not counted as one lump).
2. The overlapping day is flagged as a Double-booked conflict, exactly as it would be for standalone shifts.
3. The detail modal shows that single day's shift (its own day and hours) while indicating it belongs to the series.
